_activity: Vocab Match — Civic Principles Named So Far
_licence: Definitions for Rule of Law, Consent of the Governed, and Representative Government copied verbatim from US11R_Glossary_v2_2026-09-02, Tier B. "Sovereignty (self-government)" definition is Sam's own, matching how Day 4 (Document 5, Identification) taught the term — no glossary entry exists for it under that exact framing.
scope_note: Limited on purpose to the four principles Unit 1 has actually named out loud by Day 10 (Rule of Law via Magna Carta/Station 1, Consent of the Governed as a Day 5 Reps term, Representative Government via Document 17, and Sovereignty via Document 5's Identification debut) — not the full 14-principle Tier B list, most of which the course hasn't reached yet.
intro: Match each principle to its definition.

right.label: No one is above the law; leaders and citizens alike are bound by it
A government is just only with the agreement of the people it governs
Citizens elect officials to make decisions on their behalf
A people's right to govern themselves, free of outside control

rationale.a: Rule of Law — even a king is bound by it; Magna Carta is the unit's own example (Station 1).
rationale.b: Consent of the Governed — a Day 5 Reps term, pointed at directly before Document 6.
rationale.c: Representative Government — the principle Document 17 #4 names by name on Day 10.
rationale.d: Sovereignty — the Identification debut on Document 5, Day 4; accept self-government as the working definition taught in class.
